origin: Must be specified separately (e.g. Earth center or Solar System Barycenter)
description: SPICE inertial frame aligned with Earth mean equator and dynamical equinox of J2000; frame name alone does not specify vector origin
use: Canonical candidate for orbital/spacecraft state exchange when source uses J2000
conversion: Use SPICE pxform for position and sxform for state (position+velocity) frame transforms
caution: Do not silently rename a dataset ECI/ICRF; retain exact source frame and origin metadata

description: Mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000
use: Accept only when source explicitly labels its data ECLIPJ2000
conversion: Transform with SPICE using loaded frame definitions/kernels
caution: Not interchangeable with J2000; do not mix vectors without a transform

use: Body-fixed positions, longitude/latitude context where supported by loaded orientation kernels
conversion: Use frame transform at the requested epoch with appropriate PCK data
caution: Orientation accuracy depends on the loaded PCK/orientation model

use: Lunar surface coordinates/illumination context where needed by other module
conversion: Use frame transform at requested epoch and correct lunar orientation kernel
caution: Not the same as lunar principal-axes frames such as MOON_PA

use: Mars surface coordinates/landing interface owned by other researcher
conversion: Use frame transform at requested epoch with PCK model
caution: Surface/landing frame specifics must be agreed with the landing module owner

description: Terrestrial reference frame used by some SPICE Earth station/orientation products
conversion: SPICE frame transformations require the relevant Earth orientation data
caution: Do not use as synonym for geodetic WGS84 coordinates

description: Geodetic latitude, longitude and ellipsoidal height on WGS84
conversion: Convert geodetic coordinate to Earth-fixed Cartesian using ellipsoid, then to inertial frame at launch epoch
caution: Not an inertial frame and does not itself specify an Earth orientation transform

description: Three.js scene coordinates; positive Y is the default Object3D up direction
use: Rendering only after physics-frame conversion and local-origin rebasing
conversion: Apply explicit axis mapping, render-origin subtraction and scene scale
caution: Never calculate orbital dynamics directly in scene coordinates or treat scene units as km
